title: Longest Word in Dictionary through Deleting
summary: Given a string and a list of words, identify the longest word from the list that can be formed by removing characters from the string.
statement: Given a string and a list of words, identify the longest word from the list that can be formed by removing characters from the string. If multiple words meet this criterion, select the one that is lexicographically smallest. If no word can be formed, return an empty string.
constraints: All characters are lowercase English letters. Select a dictionary word by deleting zero or more characters from s without reordering.
Choose maximum length first, then lexicographically smallest among ties. Return the empty string if no word is possible.
hints: A dictionary word is possible exactly when it is a subsequence of s.
Use a pointer into each word while scanning s. Compare candidates by length before alphabetical order.
Advance the candidate pointer only on equal characters; after a full match replace best for a longer word or a lexicographically smaller equal-length word.
A match need not be contiguous. Do not return the first possible word, and do not sort by alphabetical order before prioritizing length.
editorial: The earliest possible match for each next character leaves at least as much remaining text as any later choice, so the pointer test finds every feasible subsequence. Scanning every dictionary entry and maintaining the best length/lexicographic pair produces the required winner. For d words, text length n, and maximum word length L, time is O(d*(n+L)) including tie comparisons; auxiliary space is O(1). The small oracle enumerates all deletions of s and selects among literal resulting strings independently.

tests.explanation: Deleting b, c, and the final a gives apple. Its length 5 beats ale and plea; monkey cannot be formed.
All three length-2 words are subsequences. Return ab: ties use alphabetical order, not dictionary order or earliest match position.
